title: NIS2 Nudge: local-language phishing drills and training records that MSPs sell to small clients
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: Small firms with fewer than 25 staff are priced out of big security-awareness tools, and many staff prefer training in Swedish or Romanian. NIS2 Nudge lets an MSP run monthly fake-phishing tests and 2-minute lessons in the local language and keeps the training records customers and regulators ask for.
hook: "Our customer's NIS2 supplier form asks for proof of staff security training. We have 14 people and no training at all."
story:
**Ioana runs a 14-person logistics firm in Cluj** that supplies a large German retailer. The retailer's new **supplier security questionnaire** asks: "Do all staff receive regular security awareness training? Provide evidence." Her MSP looks at KnowBe4, but most offers require **25 seats** and the content is in English.

Meanwhile her accountant almost paid a fake invoice that came in perfect Romanian, written by AI. Ioana wants something simple: a fake phishing email once a month, a 2-minute lesson for whoever clicks, in Romanian, and a PDF that proves it was done. Her MSP wants to resell it to all **30 of its clients** under its own name.
whyNow: NIS2 requires covered companies to train staff in basic cyber hygiene, and Sweden's Cybersecurity Act (cybersäkerhetslagen) came into force on 15 January 2026. These companies push the same expectation onto suppliers. At the same time AI lets criminals write convincing phishing in every language.
evidence: Sweden's Cybersecurity Act, implementing NIS2, came into force on 15 January 2026 and covers more organisations than the old NIS law [Transportstyrelsen]
The Swedish civil-defence agency (MCF) has prepared regulations on security measures and training under the new law [MCF impact assessment]
KnowBe4 costs about $1.63–3.75 per user per month, and most sources cite a 25-seat minimum [CostBench]
Business email compromise claims rose about 30% in the second half of 2025 [Risk & Insurance]
Coalition warns that AI phishing kits make micro businesses worth attacking [Insurance Business UK]

whyReal.title: Training evidence is now asked for
whyReal.text: NIS2 entities and their supplier questionnaires ask for proof of staff training, not just a yes.

whyReal.title: Tiny firms are priced out
whyReal.text: Seat minimums and English-only content leave 5–25 person firms without a good option.

whyReal.title: Local language matters
whyReal.text: AI-written phishing now arrives in fluent Swedish and Romanian; training should look the same.

whyReal.title: Honest weakness
whyReal.text: Phishing simulation is crowded and Microsoft bundles a tool in E5. This only works as a cheap, local-language MSP add-on.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Firms with 5–50 staff, especially suppliers to NIS2-covered companies.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The MSP (reseller) or the owner of the firm.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: Sweden and Romania/Moldova (founders' languages), then other non-English EU markets through MSPs.

solution.title: MSP adds a client
solution.text: imports staff from Microsoft 365 or a CSV, picks language and branding.

solution.title: Monthly drill
solution.text: AI writes a realistic, local phishing email based on common local scams (fake invoices, parcel notices, bank messages) from a safe library.

solution.title: 2-minute lesson
solution.text: whoever clicks sees a short lesson explaining the warning signs they missed.

solution.title: Short monthly course
solution.text: everyone gets one micro-lesson per month with a 3-question quiz.

solution.title: Evidence report
solution.text: a PDF per client: who was trained, click rates over time, ready for NIS2 supplier questionnaires and insurers.

risks.answer: Do not compete head-on; sell only through MSPs in markets where local content and no minimums matter.
Provide clear allow-listing guides for Microsoft 365 and Google; test early.
Verify domain ownership before campaigns, only send to imported staff of verified domains, log everything.
Make the MSP the customer so one sale brings many clients.

questions: Do any of your clients' customers or insurers ask for staff training evidence?
Which training tool do you offer today, and why don't small clients buy it?
In which language do your clients' staff prefer training?
Has a client fallen for a phishing or fake-invoice email in the last year?
Would you resell a $2/user tool with no minimum under your own brand?

numbers.competition: Crowded; gap is local language + no minimum
